title: Babcock to expand Horn Island aviation base in Australia
summary: The project aims to strengthen support for Australian Border Force operations in the strategically important region.
body_markdown:
Babcock Australasia (Babcock) is investing $10 million to expand its aviation base at Horn Island in Queensland’s remote Torres Strait, strengthening support for Australian Border Force (ABF) operations in the strategically important region.


After more than 30 years’ operating in partnership with the ABF, Babcock will start construction on a second, purpose-built facility to complement the company’s existing Horn Island hangar. Entegra Projects will lead the construction.


The brand-new hangar can accommodate up to three medium-sized helicopters and includes crew rest areas, briefing facilities, and climate-controlled storerooms. It will also provide floor space and equipment to conduct on-site aircraft heavy maintenance, with room to support potential future growth in the region.


Project works are underway, including detailed design and coordination with the Torres Shire Council. The new hangar will be integrated with the existing facility, which will also undergo maintenance and upgrade works to support Babcock’s current Queensland Health contract. Aeromedical operations will continue throughout construction, ensuring there is no interruption to the delivery of critical, lifesaving services to communities across the region.


The new facility forms part of Babcock’s broader investment in the region as part of the recently awarded $250 million, eight-year contract with the ABF. The program is delivering two new Airbus[H145](https://helitrader.com/for-sale/helicopters/airbus/h145) D3 helicopters into service, enhancing surveillance and response capability in the region.


The new aircraft are currently being modified by Babcock’s Design and Completions Team in the U.K., drawing on the depth of the company’s global expertise to deliver advanced capabilities for the ABF. Babcock Australasia will recruit 16 new staff, including pilots, surveillance crew and engineers to support the new ABF contract and entry into service is expected in early 2027.


Babcock’s service provides aerial surveillance and logistic support missions on behalf of the ABF including the detection and monitoring of vessels, rapid movement of personnel and equipment, and direct support to on-water operations targeting illegal foreign fishing, unauthorised arrivals and pollution incidents.


Babcock Australasia Acting Chief Executive Officer Leah Grantham said:


“Babcock’s investment in a new multi-million dollar hanger underscores our long-standing commitment to supporting the Australian Border Force and the broader Torres Strait community in one of the most strategically important and operationally demanding regions in Australia.


“Our new investment strengthens our operational capability with expanded capacity, advanced maintenance infrastructure and room to grow, while also creating skilled jobs and bringing aviation expertise to a region critical to Australia’s national security.”


*This press release was prepared and distributed by Babcock Australasia.*
